messages:
ravi: Quick update from the int8 bring-up on nova10b with KV-cache enabled. Cost down ~20% vs fp16 but we see a quality dip on long-context docs (>2k tokens). Initial numbers below, need product/GTN guidance on routing tradeoffs.

anya: Can you paste the run id and a short metric breakdown by context length?

ravi: Run: run_20240420_int8_kv_v1
```
> baseline: nova10b fp16
> quant: nova10b int8-w-kv
> buckets: <=512, 512-2048, >2048
> cost delta (tokens): -20% overall
> latency p95: fp16 180ms -> int8 160ms
> QA EM change: <=512 0.0%, 512-2048 -1.2%, >2048 -3.8%
> Rouge-L (summarization) change: <=512 -0.1, 512-2048 -0.6, >2048 -2.1
```

bench-bot: CI summary: throughput +12%, cost/unit -20%, fallbacks triggered: 7/1200 requests (>2k).

sam: Hmm 3.8% EM drop on >2k is noticeable. Do we have the prompt types for those long docs? Are they retrieval-augmented QA or open-ended summarize?

ravi: Mostly RAG+QA (multi-doc). Long queries have repeated KV hits so int8's compress/rounding seems to lose some fine-grained evidence selection.

maria: For GTN, product cares about user-visible regressions. 3-4% EM on long RAG could be unacceptable for search/answers. But for chat summaries maybe tolerable. Suggest we split by route: short/LLM completions -> int8, long-RAG -> fp16.

anya: Agreed. Can we build a quick cost-vs-quality decision threshold? e.g., route to fp16 if prompt_length + docs_tokens > 1800 OR if task==qa_rerank.

ravi: I ran a simple threshold sweep:
```
threshold tokens | pct routed to fp16 | net cost delta | net EM delta
1500            | 18%                 | -12%           | -0.9% (vs always-fp16)
1800            | 11%                 | -15%           | -1.6%
2200            | 5%                  | -18%           | -2.9%
```
(EM delta is regression relative to fp16 baseline when using threshold routing)

eval-bot: Per-eval heatmap uploaded: https://redwood-internal/eg/runs/run_20240420_int8_kv_v1 (summary table attached in run) :thumbsup:

sam: Product ask: can we auto-fallback for low-confidence outputs? If we can detect low-confidence QA answers and re-run on fp16 only for those, unit-econ could be close to int8 while limiting visible regressions. Thoughts?

ravi: We tested confidence gating (max-logit + top-2 delta) on a sample: gating re-run rate ~6% of long requests, recovers ~70% of EM delta. Implementation cost modest in runtime routing.

maria: That sounds promising. Proposed recommendation for GTN:
- Default: enable int8-w-kv for all non-RAG endpoints (saves ~20%).
- For RAG/long-context endpoints: use token-threshold route to fp16 (1800 tokens default).
- Add confidence-gating re-run to capture most regressions with small re-run rate (~6%).

anya: Can you produce a short scorecard (one-pager) with exact numbers and suggested rollout flags? We can present to PM + GTN next week. Keep it focused: unit-econ impact, user regression risk, rollout plan.

ravi: Will do. Ill include run artifacts, delta table, and a minimal rollout playbook (canary + 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with auto-fallback). ETA EOD tomorrow.

bench-bot: Note: adding confidence re-run increases p95 latency for gated requests by ~2x on re-run, but overall p95 across traffic unchanged (re-run rate low).

sam: Thanks all. If the scorecard shows the recoverable fraction is >60% with <10% re-runs, I'm pro routing. :+1:

maria: Same. Also add a note about analytics hooks to monitor user-visible regressions (sli: answer correctness, re-run rate, fallback latency).

ravi: Will add analytics + alerting thresholds. Posting draft once ready.

maria: ack :eyes:\"
